text:
marta: Incoming from a customer, they're seeing tool calls fail after we rolled model v2.5 this morning. Customer says: tool selection changed and schema validation errors. Full thread below.

alex: can you paste the error payload they get?

marta: here's the request and response they recorded (redacted api key):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-v2.5","input":"Summarize...","tools":[{"name":"invoice_lookup","schema":{"required":["user_id","invoice_id"]},"args":{"invoice_id":"1234"}}]}'
```

marta: response:
```json
{"error":{"code":"tool_schema_error","message":"Missing required field: user_id","details":{"tool":"invoice_lookup","model_routing":"redwood-v2.5"}}}
```

priya: interesting — the payload is missing user_id but they claim this worked before v2.5. Did we change default tool selection behavior?

alex: v2.5 introduced new tool selector heuristics. We also deployed selector tuning in canary earlier at 07:10 UTC. Selector can prefer namespaced tool variants (invoice_lookup_v2) if available. If model emits slightly different tool_choice token, it may pick a variant with a stricter schema.

leo: customer also reported latency spikes and a bunch of 401s around the same window. Could be unrelated but worth checking auth rotation. opsbot, pull logs for customer org: org-879, timeframe 07:00-08:00 UTC.

opsbot: Logs pulled: 1125 entries for org-879 between 2024-11-12T07:00:00Z and 2024-11-12T08:00:00Z. Summary: 78 tool_schema_error, 34 auth_failed, median p50 latency 420ms -> 980ms spike at 07:12 UTC, billing unit spike +42% at 07:13 UTC.

marta: customer says the model started emitting a different tool signature. They saw tool name "invoice.lookup" in one trace and "invoice_lookup" in another, and the chosen variant enforced user_id.

priya: can we repro locally by forcing the model to pick variant? Try rolling request to v2.5 with prompt that triggers invoice lookup and see tool selection token.

alex: I repro'ed: with v2.4 the model emitted `tool_call: invoice_lookup` and args included user_id. With v2.5 sometimes it emits `tool_call: invoice.lookup` (dot) and the runtime mapped that to invoice_lookup_v2 which has required user_id. If the caller omitted user_id, runtime returns schema error instead of falling back.

jamie: product: did we intend the selector to map dot to v2 variant? That sounds like routing mismatch.

priya: not intended. Selector update included fuzzy mapping, but mapping table didn't account for dots vs underscores. Regression.

leo: ops implication: until we fix mapping, customer traffic will see schema errors and increased token usage (retries), causing billing spikes. Suggest mitigation: 1) route org-879 to v2.4 rollback, 2) add a compatibility mapping on the runtime to treat dot/underscore as alias, 3) quick fix: transform tool args server-side to insert user_id if present in session context.

alex: I can push a patch to runtime aliasing now (small change) but may take 20-30m to build+deploy. For immediate relief, recommend pointing their traffic to dedicated fallback model redwood-v2.4 for that org (no infra change).

marta: customer asked about rolling back — they prefer we do server-side rollback for them. They already rotated a key and saw 401s while we were diagnosing; looks like rotation overlapped with rollout, causing auth failures for a short window.

leo: 401s were at 07:11-07:14 UTC. Sounds like they rotated their KMS and then calls started failing while retrying with old key. Not our fault but we should coordinate.

jamie: decision: do canary rollback for org-879 to v2.4 immediately + runtime alias patch queued. Keep monitoring billing and error rate.

priya: steps I ran to repro (for eng):
1) send sample prompt that triggers invoice lookup.
2) force model param `model=redwood-v2.5` and `deterministic=false`
3) observe tool_choice token in stream and resulting mapping.
Example request:
```json
{"model":"redwood-v2.5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Find invoice 1234 for my account"}],"tools":[{"name":"invoice_lookup","schema":{"required":["user_id","invoice_id"]}}]}
```
Observed stream snippet: "tool_choice":"invoice.lookup" then runtime chose `invoice_lookup_v2` -> schema error.

alex: I'll open a deploy with alias mapping (dot -> underscore) and add a fallback path to try invoice_lookup (legacy) when v2 variant fails schema validation. Also will add a quick canary rollback route for org-879.

marta: customer update sent: they appreciate quick action, asked for ETA. Can we give 30-45m?

leo: I'll run rollback and monitor: starting now. Will post when complete.

opsbot: Rollback action: routing override applied -> org-879 -> redwood-v2.4. Change id r-23910.

leo: rollback complete at 07:26 UTC. Error rates for org-879 dropped to normal baseline within 3 minutes. Billing spike stopped.

marta: customer confirmed success, still wants root cause and timeline for runtime patch.

alex: runtime alias patch PR #4821 opened, target deploy in next cycle (44m), will expedite and notify when live.

jamie: follow-up: we need a postmortem entry (why selector mapping change shipped without alias tests). I'll open a short incident doc and assign action items: add integration test for tool name normalizations, make canary routing more conservative.

marta: leaving thread — will send the customer the rollback confirmation and monitoring screenshots. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
